items.item_text: Board certification by the American College of Laboratory Animal Medicine, or eligibility to take the ACLAM board exam.

Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree (DVM) from a recognized and accredited school of veterinary medicine. Licensed DVM in the state of California (or able to attain a CA license within 6 months from date of hire).
Experience in medical primatology as it applies to the diagnosis, surgical procedures, and medical treatment of nonhuman primates.

Applied experience of institutional, local, state, national and international rules and regulations governing the use and care of nonhuman primates (USDA Animal Welfare Act, ILAR Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals, Endangered Species Act, FDA Good Laboratory Practice Regulations, and California Public Health Law).
Experience in preventive medicine programs required for laboratory housed non-human primates, including vaccination, parasitology, bacteriology, and virology screening programs.
Experience in investigator project support including participation in experimental protocols, research design and laboratory-directed activities.

Experience in primate clinical service support to Principal Investigators including participation in experimental research designs and clinical animal protocol development and consultation, and laboratory animal medicine directed activities.

Reporting to Associate Director of Veterinary Resources and under general direction, provide all aspects of veterinary health care. This includes preventive medical care, surgery, diagnostic imaging, pharmacology, anesthesia, routine animal care, and emergency and critical care. Tasks include physical exam, diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring of progress of animals on treatment. Duties include: Manage and oversee Hospitals (SPF/PDG/Conventional) and coordinate workflow and supervision of assigned Animal Health Technicians (AHTs) with AHT Supervisor, including performance management, addressing their questions, providing any needed clinical support or technical training of care procedures, protocols, and making sure all of work is completed in accordance with NBRI Animal Healthcare standards, regulatory requirements, and internal standard operating procedures. Evaluate complex metabolic cases such as diabetics, water restricted animals, kidney transplants, etc., as necessary. Perform all clinical procedures including laceration repair and treatment of trauma, fluid therapy, reproductive assessments, diagnostics (ultrasound, radiology, and clinical lab result assessments), clinical surgery and orthopedic surgery (internal fixation of fracture), etc. File and document laboratory results and provide documentation and maintenance of medical records and long-term outpatient records (particularly for outdoor animals on long-term treatments and monitoring). Provide onsite shift hours and on call hour coverage as well as participate in research support activities. Review records for non-breeders as required by Research Services. Write shift and case management summaries of both planned and unanticipated activities that occur during weekend/holiday shifts. Provide veterinary support services to research investigators, collaborating with research investigators in scientific research in the design, implementation, interpretation and communication of research projects. Perform management-related tasks under the general direction of senior veterinary staff. Provide and maintain wed-based surgical training modules for visiting surgeons and surgeon’s assistants. Provide support and training to students, visiting veterinarians, UCD residents, rotating Laboratory Animal Medicine residents, and clinical veterinary technicians in all aspects of primate medicine. Oversee assigned pre-project/pre-shipment physical exams; review management areas and their cases (i.e., 20% weight loss, prolonged menses, chronic diarrhea, diet manipulation, etc.). The incumbent in this position has management responsibilities of the Hospitals (Conventional, PDG and SPF) and Surgery as well as actively participates in research support procedures and experimental surgeries. Provide general support to the Center by reviewing IACUC protocols; providing input to and creating policies, guidelines, and algorithms; creating and editing standard operating procedures as needed; and managing the Center's controlled substance inventory. Participate in various Management Committees and Groups including the Relocation Committee, BMBC group on fracture management, and specific laboratory meetings). Collaborate with veterinarians and investigators at other Primate Centers as applicable.
